title: Sandboxing and running suspicious files in isolation

videos.script: A file arrives. Somebody needs to open it. Nobody can say whether it is safe. {{walls}} A sandbox runs a program in a smaller world than the machine it is on. Fewer files, no network, none of the system's powers. {{script}} In this lesson you write a suspicious file yourself, harmless, but shaped like trouble. It looks for keys, writes to the system, and calls another machine. {{sandbox}} Then you run it inside walls that systemd builds in a second, and watch every attempt fail. {{trace}} With a trace, you see what it tried and what the kernel answered. {{portal}} Last, the same walls go around the firm's own portal, and a score shows how much it was allowed before.
